key_insight: A steric-engineered ternary-solvent strategy produces hybrid perovskite monolayers exceeding 1,000 µm² in lateral area, enabling lithography-free, low-static-power optoelectronics.
engineering_relevance: Large ultrathin crystals enable solvent-free shadow-mask contacts, avoiding lithography-related chemical degradation while supporting low-dark-current planar devices.
method: Combine alcohol cosolvents and an amine additive to suppress out-of-plane stacking.
Control precursor solvation and edge-mediated transport through alcohol chain length and solvent volatility.
Fabricate isolated ultrathin perovskite channels using physical shadow masking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports dark currents of 10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹³ A, approximately 0.2 pW static power at 5 V, a 250-fold reduction versus drop-cast films, and a light-to-dark current ratio of 430.
watch_item: The abstract reports optoelectronic devices, not AI methods or solar-cell efficiency; manufacturing yield and long-term stability remain unestablished.
paper_title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
